P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but notes not read back, and the one detail he did have was wrong: 'don't know why it says California on my notes.' Frame was three-part — 'the call is pretty basic, dude. Let's just see where you're at. See if we can get you to where you want to go. If so, we can talk about the coaching' — no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement sought only as 'Alrighty', answered 'Cool.' Open question ran clean: 'What was you hoping we could potentially help you with, man?'

P2.evidence: Weight asked directly ('How much do you weigh now?' → 246.6) but age and height never asked — age only surfaced because the prospect mentioned his birthday. Work never asked; retirement from the Navy and CBP was volunteered. Surgical history volunteered, and the rep repeated it back and asked one good follow-up — 'does it restrict you at all or any pain that comes with it' — but never asked about health conditions generally, hereditary risk, the shoulder problem or the daily NSAID, all of which the prospect raised unprompted. Training asked twice and clarified ('Kettlebells aside, are you doing any dumbbell stuff') but no typical week or actual days trained. Diet asked well: 'What kind of stuff are you eating in terms of food choices?' Results from current training never asked despite a volunteered plateau. Sleep and energy never touched.

P3.evidence: Aesthetics probed loosely — 'is there anything else which is important for you in terms of goal or is it just weight loss' — which produced a good list. Bridge to the deeper driver ran well: 'I'm curious, what was the change for you that's like, I'm going back after, I'm getting all my back?', which surfaced the dress-blues story at a friend's funeral. That was the emotional core of the call and the rep did not drive it anywhere — no 'what does that do for you', no 'who else does that impact', no legacy or identity thread, despite the prospect being a never-married 66-year-old retiree for whom identity is plainly the whole motive. Reflect-back attempted early and mis-aimed: 'you look back, you're like, damn, dude, I was 280 shredded' — the prospect corrected him ('I don't want to be 280').

P4.evidence: The prospect volunteered a full failure inventory — CrossFit for eight months to a plateau, P90X, intermittent fasting, Planet Fitness, meal-delivery services — and the rep asked not one question about any of it. Never asked what happened, why it did not stick, or what is actually in the way. The root cause was never named, so the offer had no diagnosed problem to solve.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame at all. The two-year question was never asked of a 66-year-old who had just said 'I don't want to end up sitting on the sofa like a lot of people do' — the cost of inaction was handed over and left on the table. No settle-for question, no 'why not', no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The rep substituted a content-alignment question — 'Does that align with you, with kind of what you're looking for? All right, let's talk about the coaching' — and went straight into the philosophy and then price. Neither the belief question nor the all-in question was asked, and when hesitation surfaced later he did not return to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: Close was attempted, so the phase applies. No payment collected. No onboarding call with Trevor scheduled — it was described in detail but never booked, which left the prospect with nothing on his calendar. Agreement was sent mid-call and arrival confirmed ('Trevor Shan. Yep, that's the one.') but the rep explicitly did not have him sign on the call: 'that's signable. You can sign that before you pay as well.' Welcome email, Skool community link and onboarding questionnaire were never mentioned.

objection_plays.detail: Money surfaced twice — how payment works, and whether to load a card at 24-31% APR or draw from a retirement fund. The rep did run one scripted move, breaking the payment up. He ran none of the rest: no isolation ('Finances aside — nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), no SHOULD-I / HOW reframe, no permission question for an honest financial conversation, and no financial picture whatsoever — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no card count, no available credit, no investments, despite the prospect volunteering that he has retirement funds and a financial advisor. Instead of qualifying capacity he cut the entry price, twice, unprompted.

The prospect asked to read the agreement, consult his financial company and come back the following week. None of the OA moves ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually preventing you from getting started'. The rep reframed the delay as logistics, asked one soft hesitation question, and then filled twelve minutes with unrelated stories before ending the call.

A clear fear/doubt trigger: 'there's a lot of scammers out there' and 'I don't know you'. The rep responded structurally rather than with the play — emailed the agreement live from Trevor, confirmed arrival, and invited due diligence. Effective, but none of the scripted moves ran: no certainty question, no pleasure/pain framing, no bridge, plane or burned-before analogies. The doubt was still live at the end of the call.

Clinical-fit trigger with no scripted play. Two multi-level lumbar decompression/discectomy procedures, an L5-S1 fusion, and daily oral diclofenac for shoulder pain, disclosed to a rep who wrote the levels down and then estimated a 25-35 lb starting bell and a guaranteed +20 lb progression on every movement. The playbook offers no screening path and none was improvised — no question about whether a clinician had cleared loaded ballistic work. This is the script gap identified in the Tyron Giuliani call, recurring in a higher-risk form.

notes: Strong rapport and a fluent, well-structured pillar presentation, sitting on top of almost no discovery: no past-attempts phase, no consequence frame and no commitment check, so when price landed there was nothing built to hold it. Two coachable priorities — run P4 and P5 before presenting, and stop discounting the entry point in place of taking a financial picture ($6,000 to $3,000 to $1,200 in ten minutes, all rep-initiated).
